## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 11, titled *Kosiya*, sets out the disciplinary rule prohibiting a Buddhist monk from making a rug or blanket containing silk [SuttaCentral]. Under this training rule, any monk who manufactures a blanket incorporating silk commits an offence that entails forfeiture (*nissaggiya*) of the object and formal confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. Complete modern translations cataloged on SuttaCentral include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali alongside versions in four other modern languages [SuttaCentral].

This rule belongs to an established set of rug- and robe-making provisions preserved widely across early monastic lineages. SuttaCentral identifies direct parallels in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Np 11) and *Parivāra* (Np 11), alongside corresponding Prātimokṣa rules and Vibhaṅga expositions in Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka (Np 21), Mahāsāṅghika (Np 13), Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya recensions extant in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus registers 453 Pali-internal reuse passages across 102 texts, consisting principally of shared procedural, word-commentary, and relinquishment formulas shared with adjacent blanket rules—notably Bu-Vb Np12 (§1.20–2.2.11), Bu-Vb Np13 (§2.1.8–2.2.7.1), Bu-Vb Np14, and Bu-Vb Np15 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the rule across languages with sections of the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003, D0003-2) and the Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu*, corroborating SuttaCentral's curated parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
